questions.question: What must be true of corresponding angles in similar triangles?
choices: They differ by the scale factor

questions.question: What describes corresponding side lengths in similar figures?
choices: They differ by a fixed additive amount

questions.question: A side grows from 4 units to 12 units. What is the scale factor from the original to the image?
Which criterion can prove triangles similar using angles alone?
A figure is enlarged by a scale factor of 2. What happens to its perimeter?
A figure is enlarged by a scale factor of 3. What happens to its area?
A scale factor of 1/2 produces what type of image?
choices: A reduction with half the corresponding lengths
An enlargement with twice the lengths
A congruent copy with unchanged lengths
A reduction with half the corresponding angles

questions.question: Why do similar triangles not always have equal areas?
choices: Similarity changes the number of sides
Similar triangles always have different shapes
Their side lengths may have a scale factor other than 1

questions.question: Similar triangles have corresponding sides 5 and 15 units. If another side of the smaller triangle is 7 units, what is its corresponding larger side?
A drawing uses 1 centimeter for 4 meters. What actual length does 6 centimeters represent?
A triangle with sides 3, 4, and 5 is compared with one having sides 6, 8, and 10. What is true?
choices: The triangles are similar with scale factor 2
The triangles have different angle measures
The triangles are similar with scale factor 3

questions.question: What happens to angle measures under a dilation with positive scale factor?
choices: They are multiplied by the scale factor
They are divided by the scale factor

questions.question: Two similar polygons have side-length scale factor 4 from smaller to larger. What is the ratio of larger area to smaller area?
Why is increasing every side length by 3 units not generally a dilation?
choices: Adding a positive number always changes angles to 90°
Dilations allow only scale factors less than 1
A dilation must increase lengths by the same number of units

questions.question: A model is 1/20 the linear size of a building. If the model is 0.6 meters tall, how tall is the building?
A 2-meter pole casts a 3-meter shadow. At the same time, a tree casts a 12-meter shadow on level ground. Assuming similar triangles, how tall is the tree?
A rectangle is scaled by a factor of 1/3. If its original area is 81 square units, what is the new area?
Two similar solids have linear scale factor 2 from smaller to larger. What is the ratio of larger volume to smaller volume?
Two similar triangles have areas 16 and 64 square units. What is the side-length scale factor from the smaller to the larger?
An image is twice as wide but three times as tall as the original rectangle. Why is it not similar to the original?
choices: The area increased by more than 2
The width and height use different scale factors
